name: University of Birmingham Dubai
englishBachelors: Business, economics, computer science, engineering, psychology and education, awarding the University of Birmingham degree.
note: A Russell Group university's purpose-built Dubai campus, applying the same entry requirements and awarding the same degree as Birmingham. A name European employers already know.
summary: University of Birmingham degrees taught at a purpose-built campus in Dubai Academic City, with undergraduate courses in seven subject areas.
about: Students take the same University of Birmingham degree as in the UK, taught by Dubai and UK academics. Applications go direct to the Dubai campus, not through UCAS; each course sets its own IB offer.

ib.text: Set by course: Computer Science 6,6,6-6,5,5 at HL with 6 in Maths and 32+ points; Mechanical Engineering 6,6,5-6,5,5 at HL; Business Management 6,6,5 HL, 32+ points, Maths 5. Course Results: ask.

noDeadline: No closing date published; offers take up to 10 working days
notes: IB Diploma offers are set per course and shown on each course page, for example 32 points minimum with specific HL grades. The Dubai entry-requirements page gives no IB figures for the foundation courses and says to check with Admissions. No rule for IB Course Results (certificates) was found.

Applications go direct to the Dubai admissions portal, not UCAS. Undergraduates upload transcripts (predicted or first-term results are accepted, plus the GCSE certificate or equivalent), a personal statement, a reference and English proof. There is no application fee.

Closing dates: none published for September 2027 on the apply, fees or course pages. Offers are normally issued within about 10 working days of a complete application. Conditional offers need final grades before they become unconditional.

English proof (IELTS, TOEFL or PTE), by course group. Group A (Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering): IELTS 6.0, no band below 5.5, or TOEFL 80. Business: IELTS 6.5 with 6.5 in writing and speaking, or TOEFL 88. Psychology, Biomedical, Law and Media: IELTS 6.5, no band below 6.0, or TOEFL 88. No IB English waiver is stated.

Tuition for September 2027 entry: Business Management AED 146,806 a year, Mechanical Engineering AED 154,325, Computer Science AED 162,203. The course pages label these 'UK/Ireland' fees; the fees page says the first-year fee is fixed through the course and confirmed in the offer letter. It excludes visa and living costs.

Deposit: AED 7,500 for September 2027 entry (AED 5,000 for January 2027), non-refundable, deducted from tuition, due by the deadline in the conditional offer. Fees are payable in full or by instalments.

Scholarships of up to 30% are reviewed automatically after a conditional offer, with no separate application. The page says September 2027 scholarships are still under review, so the amounts for your intake are not yet published.

Many courses have an integrated foundation year, which has separate, lower entry; those are not listed here. Entry details for foundation courses and for each curriculum are shown by a country selector on the course pages.

admissionRoutes.text: Each course sets HL grades and a points minimum, typically 32 or more; the Admissions Tutor decides whether to make an offer.
No rule for IB certificates or single IB courses was found on the course or entry pages; ask Admissions.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: A three-year BSc covering algorithms, AI, systems and cyber security, accredited by the British Computer Society.
programmes.overview: You study programming in Java, then C and functional languages, with core modules in algorithms, computer systems and theory. Year 2 adds networks, security and machine learning mathematics, with a team project. Year 3 is a major project plus electives such as machine learning and computer vision. You may spend year 2 in Birmingham, UK, subject to attainment.
programmes.ib: 6,6,6 to 6,5,5 at HL with 6 in Maths and at least 32 points overall.
programmes.selectionNote: The Admissions Tutor reviews each application; a typical offer is not a guarantee.
